description:
FILED s484a (Opus, 2026-09-13) from the #1587 acceptance probe (row 18).
PRE-EXISTING IN FILE MODE, measured on main 2ffefb36
(scratch/s484a/probes/v1587.pl run on the base tree), so it is not the eval
collapse's -- the collapse only made the eval spelling reach the same emitter.

    package VerA 1.2;
    package VerB v1.2.3;
    package main;
    printf "A=%s B=%s Bvd=%s\n", $VerA::VERSION, $VerB::VERSION,
           sprintf("%vd", $VerB::VERSION);

    perl 5.40.3:  A=1.2 B=v1.2.3 Bvd=1.2.3
    PCL         : A=1.2 B=v1.2.3 Bvd=118.49.46.50.46.51

118, 49, 46, 50, 46, 51 are `v`, `1`, `.`, `2`, `.`, `3` -- the ORDINALS OF
THE SOURCE TEXT.  So `$VERSION` holds the seven-character string "v1.2.3"
where perl holds a v-string (the three-character string "\x01\x02\x03" with
the VSTRING magic that makes it print as `v1.2.3`).  The STRING form is right
by accident: PCL's `""` of the text is the same as perl's `""` of the
v-string, which is why `print $VerB::VERSION` agrees and only a numeric or
`%vd` use diverges.

WHERE: `Pl::Parser2::_pkg_version_forms` (extracted in s484a; the rule was
inline in `_assemble` before) emits

    (p-scalar-= |VerB|::$VERSION "v1.2.3")

because its `$ver_cl` is `($version =~ /^\d+(?:\.\d+)?$/) ? $version :
"\"$version\""` -- a v-literal fails the numeric test and is quoted as text.
PCL HAS a v-string representation already: `p-vstring-p` / the VSTRING arm of
`%p-ref-string`, and the runtime prints `VSTRING(0xâ¦)` for `\$v`.  So the fix
is to emit the v-string constructor for a `v`-prefixed or 3+-part literal
instead of a quoted string, the same value a `my $v = v1.2.3;` literal
already produces (probe that spelling first -- if the literal path is also
broken, that is the one place to fix and this follows).

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: any comparison or arithmetic on a v-string $VERSION.
`Foo->VERSION(1.0)` happens to work for the DECIMAL spelling (probed 1 on
both), so the reachable damage is the v-literal spelling, which is what
modern dists use in `package Foo v1.2.3;`.

BAR: ~8 probes vs perl (the two version spellings x {print, %vd, numeric
compare, `->VERSION(x)` accept and reject}, plus a bare `my $v = v1.2.3`
literal and a 3-part decimal `1.2.3`), corpus-diff (an emission change) +
emission-ab, a guard row in Pl/t/decl-ordering-02.t beside the s437 $VERSION
phase rows, and the full sweep only if the fix reaches `cl/`.
SIZE: S.
subject: `package Foo v1.2.3;` stores $VERSION as the literal STRING "v1.2.3", not a v-string: `sprintf "%vd", $Foo::VERSION` prints 118.49.46.50.46.51 (the characters of the text) where perl prints 1.2.3
